ceiling_search.rule: per model, ascending grid; stop at first full-GPU load failure, then binary-search the largest multiple of 8192 that loads with every layer on CUDA. Never exceed native_ctx_max; if native_ctx_max loads, the ceiling is reported as native_ctx_max (fits at native max).

bench.extra_depth: ceiling90 = round(0.9 * model ceiling); the deep-fill point (235,930 if the ceiling is 262,144). Run last; skip only if the budget hard stop would be hit.
bench.depth_limit_rule: depth + prompt_tokens + generated_tokens must be <= that model ceiling
bench.note: llama-bench sizes its own context to depth + prompt + generated; bench speed is a function of fill depth, not of the server window. Window VRAM comes from the load sweep.

cost_rule: actual running GPU-hours x RunPod advertised list price for the RTX 3090; estimate, not invoice
readiness: model counts as loaded only when llama-server /health returns HTTP 200 (not when the HTTP listener starts)
ctx_note: 16384 is a single anchor load tying back to CUDA Recipes 001; the study focus is 64K, 128K and 256K.
